verdict.wrong_value: Buggy warm-start computation of q.value and/or t.value for sum_largest(x,k) uses the k smallest entries (idx_of_smallest = sorted_indices[:k]) and initializes t only for top-k, instead of using idx_of_smallest = sorted_indices[:-k] and setting t.value = np.maximum(0, x.value - q.value). This can violate the feasibility constraint x_i <= t_i + q (for warm-start).
verdict.rationale: The evidence describes an incorrect numeric warm-start initialization in the canonicalizer for sum_largest: it computes q and t from the wrong threshold (k smallest vs k-th largest) and initializes t incompletely/incorrectly. That yields a wrong computed value/behavior and can make the warm-start primal solution infeasible (x_i <= t_i + q no longer holds, despite expected q=8.0 and t=[0,2,0,0,0,1]). The added test specifically checks warm-start feasibility for the k=2 case, consistent with a numerical correctness defect rather than API or non-numeric logic.
